title: Reduce hosted API 5xx waves by adding proxy backpressure + priority re-enqueue shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers experienced large latency spikes and 5xx clusters during tenant bursts. Investigation shows chain: upstream model shard slowdowns -> long-lived connections at the edge -> client SDK retries amplify inflight pressure -> internal connection pool starvation -> 5xx/timeouts returned to customers. This ticket implements a short-term proxy-level backpressure shim that converts overload into controlled, prioritized re-enqueue/429 behavior and a short-lived queued retry handoff to avoid retry storms. The goal is to stop escalation-visible 5xx waves while we roll longer-term runtime and scheduling fixes.
steps_reproduce: 1) Use a synthetic tenant to send 200 concurrent requests with client SDK default retry enabled. 2) Artificially slow the model worker (sleep on generation) to simulate shard slowdown. 3) Observe edge proxy connections piling up and backend pool exhaustion. 4) Observe increasing 5xx/timeouts and client retries leading to client-visible error spikes. 5) Reproduce with streaming and non-streaming payloads.
root_cause: A cascade caused by transient model-worker slowdowns combined with aggressive client-side retry semantics and lack of admission control at the front proxy. When model responses elongate beyond typical percentiles, the front proxy kept forwarding requests, exhausting connection pools and worker slots. SDK retries re-submitted work and amplified pressure; without a prioritized admission policy the system degraded into 5xx/timeouts instead of graceful shedding.
proposed_fix: 1) Implement a proxy shim that: a) maintains a small prioritized admission queue per-tenant (short TTL), b) returns 429 with Retry-After when queue is full for low-priority requests, and c) fast-paths priority tenants/requests into a protected slot pool. 2) Add a lightweight re-enqueue token mechanism: clients can optionally retry using a token returned in 429 to avoid immediate full-fanout retries. 3) Add server-side hedging knob to limit concurrent outstanding per-tenant and per-model shard. 4) Instrument metrics and dashboards to track queue depth, rejected-before-backend, and token reconsumption rate.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy shim behind feature-flag in edge-proxy for a single region and 3 low-risk tenants. Monitor for false-positives on streaming sessions. Phase 2: Expand to all hosted tenants with soft 429 sampling (log-only). Phase 3: Default-on with per-tenant opt-outs for Dedicated/private. Rollback gate: >1.5x increase in customer-visible error rate or streaming session disruption on canary will immediately disable feature-flag.
monitoring_and_kpis: - Reduce 5xx rate during injected shard slowdown by >=60% on canary tenants. - Median and 95th latency preserved for priority paths. - Queue drop (returned 429) rate under 1% of total requests in steady state. - Track Retry-After token reuse rate and overall request amplification. Dashboards: edge/queue-depth, per-tenant rejected_count, backend_pool_utilization, client_retry_amplification_ratio.
notes: This is an engineering-first mitigation to prevent customer-visible escalations while runtime kernel scheduling and model shard admission controls are improved in parallel. We expect false-positive 429s for a tiny slice during canary; design chosen to favor graceful degrade over cascading 5xx. Coordinate with Growth/Support for customer comms template.
review_feedback: PM (Lina Gomez): ensure 429 token is consumable by SDK without breaking existing idempotency guarantees.
Design (Priya Rao): confirm streaming semantics are preserved; prefer KEEPALIVE health checks over terminating streaming mid-response.
Security (Omar Farouk): review token entropy and TTL for replay safety; avoid long-lived opaque tokens
acceptance_criteria: Canary deployment returns 429 with Retry-After instead of backend 5xx during injected slowdowns.
No increase in successful-but-slower streaming session terminations on canary (>0.5% threshold).
Dashboards show backend_pool_utilization decrease and 5xx rate reduction on canary tenants.
SDK change (optional) consumes Retry-After token to retry after backoff without full-fanout

2025-02-17: Canary deploy to us-west-2 with tenant alpha-01; observed 70% reduction in 5xx during induced slowdown.
